newsitem.title: INDIA: India call money ends easy, seen firming next week.
newsitem.headline: India call money ends easy, seen firming next week.

text.p: Indian call money closed easy at 3.75-4.25 on Thursday in a squarish market, against the day's opening of 5.00-5.75 percent, dealers said.
There were some stray deals at 6.0 percent, a dealer said.
"Market was squarish, opened higher at 5.75 percent, remained inactive in the mid-session, while shot-up to 6.0 percent before closing at 4.0 percent," a dealer at state-run bank said.
Most of the deals were in the 5.00-5.50 percent band.
The next fortnight beginning on Saturday may see some tightness due to the advance tax outflow and the rates may rule in the range of 6.00-8.00 percent, a dealer said.
"The tighness if any will be restricted to the next fortnight, as the funds will come back into the system in the month of April," a dealer said.
The tax outgo is estimated at over 30.0 billion rupees.

There was no buying support in the securities market, as bankers were not ready to take additional position due to the March year-end. They also expect call rates to go up in the next fortnight, which may push the securities prices further down, Felix D'cunna, a dealer at Tower Capital & Securities said.
"The repo in the secondary market were quoted higher at 8.0-9.0 percent," D'cunna said.
The volume on National Stock Exchange fell to 610 million rupees, compared to previous 1.55 billion rupees, dealers said.
The 13.50 percent 1998 government stock fell to 103.00 rupees, from 103.06 rupees, while the 13.40 percent stock fell to 101.95 rupees, from 102.01 rupees against its previous close, dealers said.
The Bank of Madura certificate of deposits maturing in April 1997 was traded at yield of 9.95 percent, they said.
